rules.title: Metaphor Saturation Governor
rules.requirement: Detect excessive similes, metaphors, comparisons, and poetic reinterpretations. Preserve exceptional imagery while removing weaker repetitions.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Three metaphors across a 2,000-word scene; each changes what the narrator notices. Negative: Seven unrelated similes in a single short paragraph restate the same dread. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Three metaphors across a 2,000-word scene; each changes what the narrator notices.
rules.negative_example: Seven unrelated similes in a single short paragraph restate the same dread.
rules.limits: Pattern or count only: a human decides literary effect and intent.

rules.title: Figurative Language Value Test
rules.requirement: Require each major comparison to introduce a new perception, emotional implication, or narrative fact. Flag imagery that merely restates what the preceding sentence already established.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Comparison reveals that the supposedly harmless machine is operated by the child's father. Negative: The room was cold, like a cold room. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Comparison reveals that the supposedly harmless machine is operated by the child's father.
rules.negative_example: The room was cold, like a cold room.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Manuscript-Wide Repetition Detection
rules.requirement: Evaluate recurring language across the entire book, not only within individual chapters. Track expressions such as like, as if, not this but that, and repeated sentence openings.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: A repeated phrase changes meaning at the closing scene. Negative: The same 'as if' opener appears in 12 chapters without narrative purpose. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: A repeated phrase changes meaning at the closing scene.
rules.negative_example: The same 'as if' opener appears in 12 chapters without narrative purpose.
rules.limits: Pattern or count only: a human decides literary effect and intent.

rules.title: Metaphor Family Registry
rules.requirement: Track recurring image families—machines, wounds, clocks, legal documents, temperature, breathing, and similar devices. Distinguish intentional motifs from exhausted comparisons.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: The clock motif changes from comfort to warning to debt. Negative: Four clock similes mean only urgency. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: The clock motif changes from comfort to warning to debt.
rules.negative_example: Four clock similes mean only urgency.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Plain Prose Counterweight
rules.requirement: Protect direct, unadorned sentences. High-intensity prose must contain enough ordinary language for exceptional sentences to remain exceptional.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: A plain inventory sentence gives relief after an intense confession. Negative: Every sentence attempts an aphorism; scenes have no neutral register. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: A plain inventory sentence gives relief after an intense confession.
rules.negative_example: Every sentence attempts an aphorism; scenes have no neutral register.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Narrative Overexplanation Detector
rules.requirement: Identify passages where the narration interprets an image or explains an emotion the reader can already infer.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: He leaves the ring and locks the door; narration lets the reader infer rejection. Negative: He leaves the ring; narration explains in three sentences that this means rejection. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: He leaves the ring and locks the door; narration lets the reader infer rejection.
rules.negative_example: He leaves the ring; narration explains in three sentences that this means rejection.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Emotional Declaration Restraint
rules.requirement: Prioritize observable behavior, decisions, and consequences over repeated statements about what a character is feeling.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: She hides her shaking hand behind the ledger. Negative: She is scared, terrified, frightened and deeply afraid. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: She hides her shaking hand behind the ledger.
rules.negative_example: She is scared, terrified, frightened and deeply afraid.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Sentence-Rhythm Diversity Audit
rules.requirement: Detect excessive reliance on fragments, repeated short sentences, parallel constructions, and identical paragraph rhythms across chapters.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: An action sequence compresses, then opens into long aftermath syntax. Negative: Six chapters use the same seven-word fragment cadence. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: An action sequence compresses, then opens into long aftermath syntax.
rules.negative_example: Six chapters use the same seven-word fragment cadence.
rules.limits: Pattern or count only: a human decides literary effect and intent.

rules.title: Authorial Intrusion Detector
rules.requirement: Flag passages where the narrator announces the story's meaning, ending, structural importance, or intended impact without an established narrative reason.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Narrator remains inside the character's available perceptions. Negative: The narrator declares: 'This was the moment the novel became unforgettable.' An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Narrator remains inside the character's available perceptions.
rules.negative_example: The narrator declares: 'This was the moment the novel became unforgettable.'
rules.limits: Pattern or count only: a human decides literary effect and intent.

rules.title: Sensory Progression Engine
rules.requirement: Ensure recurring sensory details evolve in meaning or consequence. A metallic taste or irregular sound should not perform the same narrative function indefinitely.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: The tapping sound first comforts, then identifies an intruder. Negative: Metallic tapping is used ten times only to mean anxiety. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: The tapping sound first comforts, then identifies an intruder.
rules.negative_example: Metallic tapping is used ten times only to mean anxiety.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Descriptive Compression Operator
rules.requirement: Identify passages that can be shortened without losing necessary characterization, atmosphere, spatial orientation, or plot information.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Three sharp details establish power and room geometry. Negative: A twelve-line furniture list changes neither space nor character. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Three sharp details establish power and room geometry.
rules.negative_example: A twelve-line furniture list changes neither space nor character.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Prose Preservation Rule
rules.requirement: Never mechanically eliminate unusual language merely to satisfy a frequency target. Every prose correction must improve its surrounding passage while preserving authorial voice.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Proposed edit preserves a recurring character-specific metaphor and supplies comparative rationale. Negative: Autorewriter deletes every figurative sentence to hit an arbitrary count. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Proposed edit preserves a recurring character-specific metaphor and supplies comparative rationale.
rules.negative_example: Autorewriter deletes every figurative sentence to hit an arbitrary count.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Escalation Novelty Law
rules.requirement: Every major suspense beat must introduce a new danger, reveal a new mechanism, remove an option, or change the consequences. Repetition alone does not constitute escalation.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: The second threat removes evacuation, changing the available choices. Negative: A second identical alarm raises volume but changes no knowledge or options. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: The second threat removes evacuation, changing the available choices.
rules.negative_example: A second identical alarm raises volume but changes no knowledge or options.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Tension Plateau Detector
rules.requirement: Identify consecutive scenes that recreate the same emotional state without meaningfully advancing stakes, knowledge, or power.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: At stable dread, a scene changes political power and reader knowledge. Negative: Four adjacent scenes have equal dread and no state delta. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: At stable dread, a scene changes political power and reader knowledge.
rules.negative_example: Four adjacent scenes have equal dread and no state delta.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Threat Consequence Requirement
rules.requirement: Establish at least one concrete consequence of a major threat before relying extensively on the reader's fear of it.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Early sabotage injures a trusted courier, proving the threat's capability. Negative: A supposedly deadly system issues threats for 200 pages with no demonstrated consequence. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Early sabotage injures a trusted courier, proving the threat's capability.
rules.negative_example: A supposedly deadly system issues threats for 200 pages with no demonstrated consequence.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Threat Specificity Test
rules.requirement: Distinguish atmospheric unease from actionable danger. The reader should eventually understand what a threat can do, even when its origin remains unknown.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Danger's reach is shown before its origin is revealed. Negative: Narrator withholds both the mechanism and what anyone fears. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Danger's reach is shown before its origin is revealed.
rules.negative_example: Narrator withholds both the mechanism and what anyone fears.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Suspense Information-Asymmetry Engine
rules.requirement: Track what the reader, protagonist, allies, and antagonists know. Use those differences deliberately to produce suspense, surprise, and dramatic irony.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Reader knows the guard was bribed; protagonist still trusts him. Negative: Character inexplicably knows the guard was bribed without receiving the clue. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Reader knows the guard was bribed; protagonist still trusts him.
rules.negative_example: Character inexplicably knows the guard was bribed without receiving the clue.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Earned Mystery Doctrine
rules.requirement: Withhold explanations without withholding essential orientation. A reader may be uncertain about the answer while still understanding the question.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Reader understands the mystery question while the answer remains hidden. Negative: Missing subject, location and causal question make every scene incomprehensible. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Reader understands the mystery question while the answer remains hidden.
rules.negative_example: Missing subject, location and causal question make every scene incomprehensible.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Mystery Debt Ledger
rules.requirement: Track significant questions raised, clues provided, partial answers delivered, and questions deliberately carried into later books. Prevent endless mystery accumulation without payoff.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Three raised mysteries close; one series thread is explicitly deferred with a concrete reason. Negative: Twelve major mysteries are opened and none receives a payoff. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Three raised mysteries close; one series thread is explicitly deferred with a concrete reason.
rules.negative_example: Twelve major mysteries are opened and none receives a payoff.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Failure-Driven Escalation
rules.requirement: Make characters' attempts to solve problems generate consequential complications. Avoid introducing danger exclusively through unrelated external interruptions.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Attempt to bypass security permanently exposes a witness. Negative: Character attempts have no effect; surprise disasters arrive arbitrarily. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Attempt to bypass security permanently exposes a witness.
rules.negative_example: Character attempts have no effect; surprise disasters arrive arbitrarily.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Antagonist Competence Standard
rules.requirement: Ensure capable opponents make intelligent decisions, anticipate plausible defenses, learn from encounters, and remain constrained by their own resources and rules.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Antagonist alters strategy after a failed trap and pays for a surveillance gap. Negative: A capable antagonist forgets the one defense shown in the prior chapter. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Antagonist alters strategy after a failed trap and pays for a surveillance gap.
rules.negative_example: A capable antagonist forgets the one defense shown in the prior chapter.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Escalation Variety Requirement
rules.requirement: Alternate physical, emotional, social, moral, informational, institutional, and relational pressure instead of increasing only one type of danger.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Moral jeopardy follows financial jeopardy, then shifts to an intimate betrayal. Negative: Eight scenes repeatedly threaten physical injury without other pressure. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Moral jeopardy follows financial jeopardy, then shifts to an intimate betrayal.
rules.negative_example: Eight scenes repeatedly threaten physical injury without other pressure.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Tension Recovery Discipline
rules.requirement: Permit genuine relief, humor, intimacy, and ordinary life between major suspense sequences. Constant maximum tension becomes emotionally flat.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: After the explosion, characters share an unguarded joke that changes their bond. Negative: Tension stays at five throughout, with no true release. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: After the explosion, characters share an unguarded joke that changes their bond.
rules.negative_example: Tension stays at five throughout, with no true release.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Chapter-Ending Integrity
rules.requirement: End chapters on earned revelations, decisions, reversals, consequences, or unresolved pressures. Do not manufacture cliffhangers by arbitrarily concealing information.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Chapter closes on a decision that creates a new obligation. Negative: Narrator cuts mid-answer only to force a page turn. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Chapter closes on a decision that creates a new obligation.
rules.negative_example: Narrator cuts mid-answer only to force a page turn.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Human Before Function Law
rules.requirement: A character's professional role or narrative archetype must never substitute for an independent personality, emotional history, personal desire, and capacity for contradiction.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: The analyst wants to reconcile with her daughter and harbors a damaging secret. Negative: The analyst's only traits are technical competence and plot function. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: The analyst wants to reconcile with her daughter and harbors a damaging secret.
rules.negative_example: The analyst's only traits are technical competence and plot function.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Personal Desire Conflict Engine
rules.requirement: Give major characters desires that can conflict with their duties, loyalties, institutional obligations, or stated principles.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Pilot wants recognition but duty requires confessing a mistake. Negative: Everyone desires only to complete the mission. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Pilot wants recognition but duty requires confessing a mistake.
rules.negative_example: Everyone desires only to complete the mission.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Costly Rule Violation Test
rules.requirement: Create opportunities for characters to break established rules for psychologically credible reasons, accepting the consequences rather than receiving automatic narrative protection.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Doctor risks a license to save a stranger and must face proceedings. Negative: Hero violates every rule with no consequence or reason. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Doctor risks a license to save a stranger and must face proceedings.
rules.negative_example: Hero violates every rule with no consequence or reason.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Distinct Character Decision Profiles
rules.requirement: Differentiate characters through the decisions they make under pressure, not merely their vocabulary, dialogue rhythms, or assigned expertise.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Two trained officers make different costly decisions under the same risk. Negative: Everyone chooses the same plan and differs only in catchphrases. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Two trained officers make different costly decisions under the same risk.
rules.negative_example: Everyone chooses the same plan and differs only in catchphrases.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Relationship Evolution Ledger
rules.requirement: Track how trust, affection, resentment, dependency, attraction, suspicion, and power change after consequential encounters.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Trust falls after betrayal and recovers only after demonstrated sacrifice. Negative: A betrayal is followed by immediate unexplained intimacy. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Trust falls after betrayal and recovers only after demonstrated sacrifice.
rules.negative_example: A betrayal is followed by immediate unexplained intimacy.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Emotional Memory Continuity
rules.requirement: Preserve the emotional residue of events across subsequent chapters. Characters must not recover from significant experiences simply because the next scene needs them functional.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Survivor's sleep and choices change after the fire. Negative: Character witnesses a death and jokes normally next chapter without residue. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Survivor's sleep and choices change after the fire.
rules.negative_example: Character witnesses a death and jokes normally next chapter without residue.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Human Stakes Translation
rules.requirement: Connect large conceptual threats to personal losses involving relationships, memories, ordinary possessions, familiar places, bodily autonomy, or identity.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Citywide network outage prevents mother reaching her missing son. Negative: Threat to the world is explained only by abstract statistics. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Citywide network outage prevents mother reaching her missing son.
rules.negative_example: Threat to the world is explained only by abstract statistics.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Character Agency Verification
rules.requirement: Ensure major turning points arise meaningfully from character decisions rather than characters merely watching external mechanisms operate.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Protagonist chooses exposure over safety, creating the climax. Negative: Victory occurs because of an accidental external reset. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.

rules.title: Competence Without Emotional Uniformity
rules.requirement: Permit skilled professionals to disagree, misjudge, become exhausted, show humor, fear embarrassment, or act irrationally without reducing their intelligence.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Brilliant analyst makes a shame-driven mistake yet remains competent. Negative: Experts behave like identical emotionally neutral calculators. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.

rules.negative_example: Experts behave like identical emotionally neutral calculators.

rules.title: Emotional Payoff Audit
rules.requirement: Verify that important losses, sacrifices, reunions, betrayals, and victories receive dramatized consequences rather than only procedural acknowledgment.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: After reunification, character grieves what was irreversibly lost. Negative: Beloved character dies and the story treats it as resolved paperwork. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.

rules.negative_example: Beloved character dies and the story treats it as resolved paperwork.

rules.title: World Rules Constitution
rules.requirement: Record what the fictional world's mechanisms can do, cannot do, require, consume, and risk. Distinguish absolute constraints from beliefs held by characters.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: The device has stable input, output, cost, and forbidden operations. Negative: Power acquires abilities without constraints as needed. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.

rules.title: Power Boundary Enforcement
rules.requirement: Prevent antagonists, technologies, magic, institutions, or supernatural systems from acquiring convenient new abilities without established causal justification.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Enemy's forbidden remote action is refused, forcing a physical incursion. Negative: Enemy uses an expressly forbidden remote attack without a retcon. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.

rules.negative_example: Enemy uses an expressly forbidden remote attack without a retcon.

rules.title: Cost Conservation Doctrine
rules.requirement: Track the consequences of extraordinary interventions. Costs cannot disappear merely because a character has completed an objective or delivered a satisfying speech.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Each resurrection drains a finite shared memory reserve. Negative: The reserve refills at chapter end for no reason. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.

rules.negative_example: The reserve refills at chapter end for no reason.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Victory Versus Closure Distinction
rules.requirement: Distinguish tactical success, strategic success, moral legitimacy, physical safety, and permanent resolution. A victory may achieve one without guaranteeing the others.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Extraction succeeds but causes political and moral damage. Negative: Narration labels operational success as total ethical closure. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.

rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Consent and Authority Conflict Model
rules.requirement: In fiction involving institutions or advanced technologies, distinguish capability, claimed authority, actual authority, and the consent of affected people.

rules.title: Canon Contradiction Classification
rules.requirement: Separate intentional paradoxes, character misinformation, unreliable narration, unresolved mysteries, and genuine authorial continuity defects.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Unreliable account is tagged as disputed, not normalized into canon. Negative: Two opposing facts silently coexist as simultaneously canonical. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.

rules.requirement: Require major fictional rules to be demonstrated through events and consequences, not explained solely through terminology, speeches, or appended technical material.

rules.requirement: Distinguish accepted science, contested hypotheses, fictional extrapolation, and invented mechanisms. Do not present scientifically unsupported claims as established physical laws in authorial exposition.

rules.positive_example: Primary case closes; a peripheral threat remains for the next book.
rules.negative_example: Nothing central resolves because the sequel must sell.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Emotional Center Protection
rules.requirement: Identify the most important human conflict beneath the speculative machinery and verify that the overarching plot does not displace it.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Climax's technology decision also resolves a mother's loyalty conflict. Negative: Final 80 pages explain machines but forget core relationship. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Climax's technology decision also resolves a mother's loyalty conflict.
rules.negative_example: Final 80 pages explain machines but forget core relationship.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Front Matter Separation
rules.requirement: Distinguish story-essential opening material from author manifestos, explanatory essays, promotional statements, and supplementary commentary. Place each where it best serves the reader.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Authorial manifesto moves outside the novel's in-world first scene. Negative: Promotional review quotes interrupt an unfolding rescue. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Authorial manifesto moves outside the novel's in-world first scene.
rules.negative_example: Promotional review quotes interrupt an unfolding rescue.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Document Placement Validator
rules.requirement: Detect glossaries, pronunciation guides, appendices, and explanatory documents placed inside narrative sequences or after the point where readers needed them.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Glossary occurs in back matter with useful cross-references. Negative: Glossary interrupts the decisive confrontation. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Glossary occurs in back matter with useful cross-references.
rules.negative_example: Glossary interrupts the decisive confrontation.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Mathematical and Symbol Rendering Verification
rules.requirement: Detect raw LaTeX fragments, malformed Unicode, escaped characters, broken equations, and damaged technical notation in publication exports.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Typeset equation round-trips exactly in exported edition. Negative: Export shows raw '\alpha' and replacement character U+FFFD. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Typeset equation round-trips exactly in exported edition.
rules.negative_example: Export shows raw '\alpha' and replacement character U+FFFD.
rules.limits: Pattern or count only: a human decides literary effect and intent.

rules.title: Publishing Metadata Completeness
rules.requirement: Check title page, copyright information, edition, ISBN when applicable, publisher information, and outstanding placeholder fields before release.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Title, edition and publisher completed; ISBN marked not applicable for draft. Negative: Print release has 'INSERT ISBN' and missing edition. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Title, edition and publisher completed; ISBN marked not applicable for draft.
rules.negative_example: Print release has 'INSERT ISBN' and missing edition.
rules.limits: Typed evidence checks assert only the declared data and its consistency, not artistic success.

rules.title: Timeline and Cross-Book Reference Proofing
rules.requirement: Check historical references, dates, chapter citations, continuity anchors, punctuation, and relationships between installments.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Cross-book reference matches verified chapter and timeline anchors. Negative: Book two cites a scene dated years before a character's birth. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Cross-book reference matches verified chapter and timeline anchors.
rules.negative_example: Book two cites a scene dated years before a character's birth.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Typesetting and Pagination Audit
rules.requirement: Evaluate page count against word count, typography, margins, line spacing, chapter breaks, widows, orphans, and readability across print and ebook formats.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: EPUB reflow verified on multiple font sizes; print margins manually checked. Negative: PDF contains clipped notation and unreadable gutters. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: EPUB reflow verified on multiple font sizes; print margins manually checked.
rules.negative_example: PDF contains clipped notation and unreadable gutters.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Independent Reader Evaluation
rules.requirement: Require human beta-reader feedback on confusion, attachment, suspense, pacing, emotional impact, and ending satisfaction. Automated scores are supporting evidence, not proof of reader experience.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Consenting independent readers report confusion and attachment against scene anchors. Negative: Creator gives the book a ten based solely on model ratings. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Consenting independent readers report confusion and attachment against scene anchors.
rules.negative_example: Creator gives the book a ten based solely on model ratings.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.

rules.title: Genre-Specific Publication Gate
rules.requirement: A novel cannot be marked publication-ready solely because grammar, style, continuity, and file checks pass. Developmental, artistic, and reader-facing assessments must be reported separately, including unresolved risks.
rules.acceptance_test: Positive: Release names open artistic concerns, reader evidence, and format proofs. Negative: Publication-ready badge issued from grammar pass alone. An evaluator must cite scene or text anchors; a raw score is insufficient.
rules.positive_example: Release names open artistic concerns, reader evidence, and format proofs.
rules.negative_example: Publication-ready badge issued from grammar pass alone.
rules.limits: Requires accountable human/editorial evidence; cannot be auto-verified.
